title: The stage-back and brief-rules tests no longer build a cold rag index of the whole kb only to read a brief line
goal: test_land_e2e.py's stage_back test and test_backlog_portable.py's brief_rules test keep every assertion but no longer pay a cold rag index build, so stage_back runs at most 6 s alone and brief_rules at most 2.5 s alone in a tests.py -k run with --durations=0; no test id is lost (perfcheck.py ids --base origin/main)

run: import re,subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/tests.py','-k','stage_back_commits or brief_rules_are','--no-reuse','--durations=0'],capture_output=True,text=True);d=[(m[1],float(m[0])) for m in re.findall(r'^(\d+\.\d+)s call\s+\S+::(\w+)',p.stdout,re.M)];s=[v for k,v in d if k.startswith('test_stage_back_commits')];b=[v for k,v in d if k.startswith('test_backlog_brief_rules_are')];print(d);sys.exit(1 if p.returncode or not s or not b or max(s)>6 or max(b)>2.5 else 0)

clauses.clause: test_land_e2e.py's stage_back test and test_backlog_portable.py's brief_rules test keep every assertion but no longer pay a cold rag index build, so stage_back runs at most 6 s alone and brief_rules at most 2.5 s alone in a tests.py -k run with --durations=0
no test id is lost (perfcheck.py ids --base origin/main)

gates.question: How do the stage-back and brief-rules tests skip the cold rag index build while keeping every assertion?
options: test side only: each test hands its pack a small planted root or an index built once, with no product change
a product seam in bl_dispatch.pack_lines that a test can turn off
gates.recommendation: test side only: each test hands its pack a small planted root or an index built once, with no product change
gates.answer: test side only: each test hands its pack a small planted root or an index built once, with no product change

notes: Premise, measured 2026-10-14 on a quiet darwin host: rag.py pack on a fresh clone builds its index cold in 5.8 s, against 0.57 s in a second clone given the first one's index (KB_INDEX; the index is keyed by content). stage_back takes 12.2 s alone, of which brief's rules pack (rag.py pack --root _self --item, run by bl_dispatch.pack_lines) is 7.1 s, while the test's brief assertions read only its stage-back lines; brief_rules takes 6.4 s alone, of which rag.py pack --root fixture is 7.1 s under the full run (its KB_INDEX is a fresh temp directory). A subprocess trace of the whole suite shows a cold pack in these 2 of 112 tests only. Under --dist load stage_back is the run's longest test (14.7 to 18.3 s). A KB_INDEX shared by every scenario of a run did not help (24.7 to 25.3 s): one cold build per run remains, and setting it for the live-kb tests made them build cold too (26.2 to 26.9 s), so the cut is per test. Precheck, 2026-10-14: under bl_base.check_env (done, review and precheck runs) KB_INDEX is the main worktree's _cache, so stage_back's pack finds a built index there: 6.74 s alone, against 12.23 s in a bare pytest run (pack 5.82 s cold); brief_rules sets its own KB_INDEX and stays cold either way (6.47 s). Both checks fail on the base, as they should.
